Whenever I'm at the gym, I always see people doing workouts incorrectly and for some reason it just bothers me. I've offered help in some areas, but I know a lot of videos say you're a douche if you try to "help". What is everyone's opinion on whether or not it's okay to talk to people about doing an exercise properly?

For me, I would prefer someone to come up to me and critique me if my form is off.
Offering help to people in the gym. Is this okay?

I have had it happen once in 8 years and it was sound advice which I follow to this day.

It is all about that person but there is no way to be sure that person wants it. I would like to know if I'm pulling awful form but then again I spotted some guy who was benching 50kg and was boasting about having benched 100kg before he took a 3 week break. He I doubt would take advice well. Stuff like if I have to do most the work on your first set you're probably starting too heavy.

Keep in mind there is a difference between doing something in a manner other than the way you would do it and doing something wrong. Just because someone does something different than you would do it doesn't make it wrong. Somebody doing something obviously dangerous, I think a comment is in order. I see young guys in the gym all the time trying to work out with way to much weight with terrible form. However, they're not going to listen to an old guy like me, I leave them alone. My SO has guys stop and try to help her all the time. She's a trained physical trainer and dance instructor, she knows what she's doing, they're just hitting on her. If you're going to say something to somebody make sure your motives are pure.
I had to bite my tongue all the time when I trained in a commercial gym. Most people don't want to hear it anyways and won't listen to you so why waste the time?
I appreciate it. I'm too stingy to pay for a personal trainer, so if I'm doing it wrong I have NFI unless someone says something or I injure myself and Google it while recuperating.

I'm open as long as someone isn't being pushy. "Hey dude, have you tried X grip? Found it works great for me" is pretty good IMO. "You are doing it all wrong, let me show you" will make me act like I didn't hear you and turn up my headphone volume.
